rpcNote: SENTRY, deliberately. Broadcast through this endpoint and never through polkachu, which accepts a transaction and then serves no receipt for it - which reads as a failure on a tx that landed, and invites a re-send. Verified 2026-09-07: eth_chainId answers 0x6f0.

external.multicall3Note: Canonical Multicall3, verified 2026-09-08 by eth_getCode on BOTH nets: 3,808 bytes at the same address on 1439 and 1776, and an aggregate3 of three ChoiceFeeController views was executed against it on 1439 and returned the right answers (335 / 2011 / 330000). It is recorded because the frontend's read client deliberately shipped with viem's `batch.multicall` OFF - its own comment says "Injective's public RPCs do not all ship a multicall3, and a missing one turns every read into a silent failure rather than a slow one. Turn it on per network once the address is in the book." This is that entry. It matters for fees specifically: a pool's PROTOCOL fee exists only on chain - the indexer cannot serve it, because ProtocolFeeUpdated never fires for a pool whose fee was set at initialize - so every pool list that wants to show a true swap fee needs one getSlot0 per pool.
external.externalNote: Every address in this group was read off chain 1776 on 2026-09-07, not copied from the testnet book. eth_getCode sizes: permit2 9,152 / wINJ 5,954 / Arachnid CREATE2 69 / Safe proxy factory 3,054 / Safe singleton L2 24,421 / Safe fallback handler 5,637 - identical to the testnet deployment's, which is the point: the whole Safe stack and Permit2 are canonical on both nets at the same addresses, so nothing here has to be deployed. The two precompiles answer eth_getCode with 0x on Injective and always will; that is expected and is not evidence of absence.
external.tokenNote: usdt / usdc / sai were each proved by calling them: symbol() and decimals() answered USDT/6, USDC/6, SAI/18 on 1776. 🔴 THE TESTNET BOOK'S TWO-USDC TRAP DOES NOT EXIST HERE. On 1439 the launchpad quotes its own tokenfactory USDC (external.padUsdc) while external.usdc is the Circle FiatToken, and both answer symbol() == 'USDC'. On mainnet the pad quotes EVM-native USDC 0xa00C59fF..., which IS this entry - the launchpad's own mainnet book, quoteAssets.USDC.pairAsset - so there is one USDC and no padUsdc key. Do not add one.
external.usdtNote: Mainnet USDT is the peggy USDT ERC20-module pair, 6 decimals. It is recorded because wINJ/USDT is the deepest INJ pair on the chain and is the obvious first seeded pool, NOT because anything is committed to it. No pool exists yet; see `pools`.

governance.governanceNote: ⛔ PHASE 1 CANNOT RUN UNTIL `create3Factory` IS FILLED, and that is deliberate - BaseScript.readAddress reverts on a null entry, so a missing address stops the run rather than deploying something wired to address(0). `safe` and `timelock` are null because script 01 WRITES them; the factory is null because it is deployed first, by plain CREATE from the nonce-0 EOA below, and its address is already known to be 0xa4753315E17b79A6f0Dc7739650D019dDD807Df5 - check the deploy against that rather than trusting the run. ✅ The signer set is no longer blocking: safeSigners and safeThreshold were settled 2026-09-08 evening (see safeSignersNote), and both deploy EOAs were generated and proved fresh on 1776 the same day. 🔑 The timelock's address is likewise already known: CREATE3 derives it from the salt and the factory alone, so with the factory fixed above it will be 0x8a3c2cDaa43D7b2D352830103eFD434E19EAbE10 - computed by running the deployed factory's own bytecode at the mainnet factory address, a method that reproduces testnet's 0xfE9811111C... exactly. That is what lets the three fork deploy configs name `poolOwner` before script 01 has ever run. 🔴 What script 01 now does with all of this, added in the 2026-09-08 audit pass: it asserts the Safe's owners and threshold and the timelock's roles and delay against this file BEFORE writing either address back, because both legs skip when the target already has code and neither used to ask what that code was.
governance.timelockMinDelayNote: 3600 = 1 hour, at launch. 🔴 THIS IS ALSO THE UNPAUSE LATENCY and a brand-new DEX carrying partner flow cannot be down for a day: pausePoolManager is role-or-owner so a monitoring key can stop swaps in seconds, but unpausePoolManager is onlyOwner and the owner is this timelock - so the delay is the floor on recovery from a pause, accidental or hostile. ⚠️ What the shorter delay costs, and it is the reason 86400 was chosen first on 2026-09-07: the delay is the window in which a hostile or mistaken proposal can be spotted and cancelled. See timelockTargetDelay for the raise to 24h that follows once the DEX is settled, and safeSignersNote for why the per-owner CANCELLER grants stopped being optional in the same decision - with only three keys, two of them one person's, an hour only helps if somebody other than the proposer can actually cancel. 🔑 Script 08 checks the LIVE getMinDelay() equals this number on every run, and enforces a one-hour floor on mainnet. The floor used to be 24 hours while this file said 3600, so the one script meant to fail loudly would have failed on a correct deploy - fixed in the 2026-09-08 audit pass (G-2). ✅ What makes both directions survivable: a pause blocks swap and donate ONLY. modifyLiquidity is not paused, so users can always withdraw liquidity while paused.
governance.timelockTargetDelayNote: The delay this deployment intends to RAISE to once the DEX is settled - 86400 = 24 hours. It is recorded rather than left as an intention because the raise is easy to keep postponing and nothing else would ever mention it: script 08 prints it as a standing note for as long as timelockMinDelay is below it. 🔑 HOW THE RAISE IS DONE: `TimelockController.updateDelay` is `onlySelf`, so it is not a call anybody makes - it is an operation the timelock schedules against ITSELF. Safe -> timelock.schedule(timelock, 0, updateDelay(86400), 0, 0, <current delay>), wait, execute. 🔴 And it is TWO changes, not one: script 08 checks the live getMinDelay() EQUALS timelockMinDelay in this file, and ForkLink.t.sol pins that number, so the same PR that executes the raise must move timelockMinDelay to 86400 here. Otherwise the next verify run goes red on a deployment that is more secure than it was.
governance.pauserNote: ⚠️ NULL, and that means NOBODY CAN PAUSE without the full timelock delay. `pausePoolManager` on both PoolManagerOwner contracts is role-or-owner, so a monitoring key holding the pause role stops swaps in seconds; `grantPausableRole` is onlyOwner and the owner is the timelock, so granting it is a scheduled operation somebody has to remember - it does not happen as part of any deploy script. Fill this with the holder's address when it is decided and script 08 will check the grant on both owner contracts and print the payload if it is missing. 🔑 What a pause actually costs, which is why granting it is cheap: it blocks `swap` and `donate` ONLY. `modifyLiquidity` is NOT paused, so users can always withdraw liquidity while paused. What it costs on the other side is the delay - `unpausePoolManager` is onlyOwner, so a compromised or careless pause key can hold the DEX down one delay period at a time. Give it to a dedicated key, never to the deployer.
governance.deployCompleteNote: FALSE until the last phase has landed, then flipped to true in a reviewed PR. It gates the STANDING-HYGIENE checks in script 08 - the per-owner CANCELLER grants, the pause role, the CREATE3 factory's whitelist and its ownership - which are required by the END of a deploy and not before it. Failing on them mid-deploy would block the very phases that still need a whitelisted deploy key, so while this is false they print as notes and the run stays green; once it is true they count as outstanding and the run fails until they are done. ⚠️ Everything else in script 08 - ownership, the timelock's roles, the Safe's owners and threshold, the delay matching this file, the launch-pool wiring - is enforced at every stage regardless of this flag.
governance.safeSignersNote: THREE addresses, threshold 2 - settled 2026-09-08 evening, superseding the 2-of-2 recorded earlier that day. 0xF9191d4E... is a voter on Choice v1's dev multisig. 🔑 That multisig is a cw3-fixed-multisig CONTRACT (code id 1) and answers {"list_voters":{}}, so the line that stood here until 2026-09-08 - that v1's signers 'CANNOT be recovered from the chain' - was wrong, and it is worth knowing why: the multisig ACCOUNT has pub_key null, the CONTRACT does not care. Injective keys are eth_secp256k1, so every 0x here is the same key as its inj1... form and can sign a Safe transaction as-is - MetaMask on the same seed, or the Ledger Ethereum app, which is what Injective's own Ledger support already uses. One of the three is a FRESH key: read off 1776 on 2026-09-08 it was nonce 0, no code, and pub_key still null - it has NEVER SIGNED, so the chain cannot show who holds it. That is what the proof-of-control ceremony before script 01 exists for, and it is the only evidence of control that will ever exist for it. 🔴 THE RISK THIS SHAPE ACCEPTS, written down so it is a decision and not a discovery: TWO OF THE THREE KEYS ARE HELD BY ONE PERSON, who can therefore pass any proposal alone. Stated and accepted 2026-09-08. Two things stop that from also being a single point of failure, and both are steps rather than properties: every owner is granted CANCELLER_ROLE on the timelock, so any ONE of the three can stop a proposal inside the delay; and one of those two keys is to be replaced by a dedicated hardware device with a single Safe swapOwner - one transaction, no redeploy - before the DEX carries size. 🔒 DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS FILE, BECAUSE THIS REPO IS PUBLIC: which owner is which, what each key is stored in, and the on-chain reading of Choice v1's two multisigs. Those are custody questions, and publishing them would name the softest of three keys that jointly own the whole DEX. They are recorded in the private security audit (SECURITY_AUDIT_2026-09-08.md, G-1) in the workspace repo, which is where a reader with a need to know will already be. ⚠️ Do NOT reuse the testnet signers 0x8BDa0790... / 0xF48390Bb... / 0xF7Ca1E12... - those are local keystores on a development machine, which is the correct shape for 1439 and the wrong shape for a Safe that owns the timelock that owns the whole DEX.
governance.create3DeployerEOANote: 🔴 A DEDICATED EOA WHOSE FIRST-EVER MAINNET TRANSACTION IS THE Create3Factory DEPLOY. Plan D2, corrected: Create3Factory's constructor does `Ownable(msg.sender)` and `isUserWhitelisted[msg.sender] = true`, so deploying it THROUGH the Arachnid CREATE2 deployer makes the owner and sole whitelisted user 0x4e59b448..., a stub that can call nothing - the factory is bricked permanently. Reproduced on anvil 2026-09-04. Deploy it by plain CREATE from nonce 0 instead; upstream's own 01_DeployCreate3Factory.s.sol asserts nonce == 0 for the same reason. The factory address is then a pure function of this EOA, since CREATE(eoa, 0) depends on nothing else. ✅ GENERATED 2026-09-08 and PROVED FRESH on 1776 in the same pass: nonce 0, balance 0, eth_getCode 0x. Because CREATE(eoa, 0) depends on nothing else, the Create3Factory address is already known and is 0xa4753315E17b79A6f0Dc7739650D019dDD807Df5 - check the deploy against that rather than trusting the run. 🔴 CUSTODY IS A PRECONDITION OF FUNDING, not a tidy-up afterwards: this key must sit in a keystore held like a signer's, with no other copy anywhere, BEFORE this address is funded or the factory is deployed - see create3OwnerWarning for why it is a STANDING privilege and not a one-shot deploy key. Until that has happened, treat this address as a proposal rather than a decision - regenerating it costs nothing today and costs a redeployment of everything after the first broadcast.
governance.create3OwnerWarning: 🔴 THE FACTORY OWNER IS A STANDING PRIVILEGED KEY ON MAINNET, and it is easy to read as a one-shot deploy key. Create3Factory.deploy is gated only by isUserWhitelisted and setWhitelistUser is onlyOwner, and Create3.addressOf(salt) is NOT namespaced by msg.sender - so whoever holds this key can deploy ARBITRARY CODE at ANY unclaimed CHOICE-V2 salt, including CHOICE-V2/TimelockController/1.0.0. Script 01 would then take it: its idempotency check is `if (timelock.code.length > 0) skip`, with no code-hash or role check, and it writes that address into this book. ⇒ Custody this key like a signer, and after Phase 3 transfer the factory's ownership to the timelock (it is Ownable2Step) and de-whitelist the ordinary deployerEOA.
governance.deployerEOANote: The ordinary deploy key: hot, funded with INJ, whitelisted on the Create3Factory by the owner EOA. It holds no privilege after the deploy - every contract it deploys is born owned by the timelock - so it is the one key here that may be a plain keystore. ✅ GENERATED 2026-09-08, proved fresh on 1776 (nonce 0, balance 0, no code). It needs INJ before Phase 1 and it needs whitelisting on the factory by the create3 owner key; it holds no privilege afterwards.
governance.addressParityNote: ☑ DECIDED 2026-09-07: a FRESH, MAINNET-ONLY EOA, custodied like a signer. Cross-net address parity is deliberately given up - the mainnet Create3Factory and TimelockController will NOT land on the testnet addresses. This is recorded rather than left silent because the parity WAS available and someone will otherwise assume it was missed: verified 2026-09-07, both testnet EOAs (create3DeployerEOA 0x15248340974929CeF4194a9Be763960d8A807fbc, deployerEOA 0xAcA0d67c52B503ED15706df5fE29E19677338bc6) were at NONCE 0 with ZERO balance on 1776, and 0x2Be6e98818A7CbBd1c7fD8e06A3B0449715790CD (the factory) and 0xfE9811111Cffd823aA2c1c8F31A77009BFaeDE42 (the timelock, CREATE3 off the same salt) were both EMPTY there - so reusing one would have landed both on the same addresses as testnet, which is exactly what plan D2 was designed to buy. 🔑 The reason not to is create3OwnerWarning above: the factory owner is a STANDING privileged key that can place arbitrary code at any unclaimed CHOICE-V2 salt, and the testnet key is a keystore that has lived on a development machine. Address parity is cosmetic; that is not. ⚠️ The EOA does not exist yet - this field stays null until it is generated, and Phase 1 cannot run while it is.

choice.treasuryNote: ⛔ NULL, and script 02 reverts on it - readAddress refuses a null - so this must be filled BETWEEN script 01 and script 02. It cannot be pre-filled here because it is the Safe, and the Safe's address is not known until script 01 has created it. ⇒ After script 01, copy governance.safe into this field. That is what testnet does (choice.treasury == governance.safe 0x0ee0Db41...), and it is right for the same reason: protocol revenue should land somewhere the signers already control rather than at a fresh address nobody has tested a withdrawal from. ✅ Low stakes at launch and easy to move later: with protocolFeeSplitRatio at 0 nothing is ever collected, so this address receives nothing until the fee is turned on, and setTreasury is a plain timelock call. ⚠️ It is still a CONSTRUCTOR argument to both fee controllers, so getting it wrong means a Tier-1 redeploy of both rather than a setting change - check it before broadcasting.
choice.protocolFeePolicyNote: 🔴 MAINNET LAUNCHES WITH CHOICE'S PROTOCOL FEE FULLY OFF. Decided 2026-09-08: partners route volume against their own liquidity at no protocol cost, so the only fee a pool charges is its LP leg, which a partner who IS the LP earns straight back. Both numbers are CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENTS to ChoiceFeeController (script 02 reads them from here), not post-deploy calls - under CREATE3 the controller is born owned by the factory's one-shot proxy child with the timelock only as pendingOwner, so between deployment and acceptOwnership there is nobody who could make the call, and pool creation is permissionless, so any pool opened in that window would bake in the wrong policy permanently for that pool. ⚠️ TWO numbers, not one, and the second is the one that gets missed: a DYNAMIC-fee pool never consults protocolFeeSplitRatio at all - upstream's protocolFeeForPool branches on the dynamic flag first and answers defaultProtocolFeeForDynamicFeePool, which ships at 300 (0.03%) - so zeroing only the ratio leaves a live protocol fee on every dynamic-fee pool anybody opens, silently. test/ProtocolFeesDisabled.t.sol pins both. 🔑 TURNING IT ON LATER NEEDS NO REDEPLOY, but it is two different operations: setProtocolFeeSplitRatio(330000) from the timelock restores the plan §4 tier table for pools opened AFTERWARDS, while pools that ALREADY EXIST keep the zero they were born with - a pool's protocol fee is fetched from the controller once, at initialize, and stored - so each one needs its own clFeeController.setProtocolFee(key, fee). Batch those into a single timelock operation. Note testnet deliberately runs the opposite policy (330000/300) so the fee path stays exercised and the frontend's tier table keeps being checked against a live pool.
choice.choiceNote: Nothing here is deployed. 🔑 There is NO positionLockerLegacy and NO launchFeeCrankerLegacy key, and there should never be: those exist on testnet only because a locker generation was superseded after launches had already registered into it. A fresh deployment starts with one locker generation and one cranker.
choice.treasuryBpsNote: 🔴 SHIP BOTH FEE CONTROLLERS AT treasuryBps = 10000 (everything to treasury, the burn sink never called). It is the default; keeping it is a DECISION, not inertia - see MAINNET_READINESS C3. Before it is ever lowered, confirm every fee currency is on Injective's governance-set auction-transfer denom list: a currency that is not on it accumulates at 0x1111...1111, the real ExchangeAuctionFeesAddress, where nobody holds a key. At 10000 the sink is never called and that risk cannot arise.
choice.choiceRouterNote: 🔴 SHIPS INERT. Script 07 allowlists this network's vault and nothing else, so every Pumex stage reverts VaultNotAllowed. Its production cross-vault configuration has never run on any chain (MAINNET_READINESS C2); enabling Pumex is its own change, behind the timelock, with its own small-size live route as the proof.
choice.quoteRouteAssetKeysNote: Empty on purpose. This lists BOOK KEYS, never addresses, so an asset's address lives in exactly one place - and it is only populated once a launch graduates against a quote that is not the sink's QUOTE, AND a real market exists to route through. 🔴 The testnet SAI and padUSDC routes were seeded at an ASSUMED price because no pool existed; on mainnet a route must come from a real market, or the quote asset should not be accepted at all.

launchpad.launchpadNote: ⛔ BLOCKED ON AN UNSETTLED DECISION, and it is not this deploy's to make. MAINNET_READINESS Part 2 opens on it: is the launchpad's mainnet a NEW core, or the live core 0xd948740da926E8908A08414879490d0D8F96D463? The plan's own logic points at a new core (option A) - it is the only way the A2/C3/B7 quote gates ship, the pad has done exactly this cutover once already with a written runbook, and the 177 live launches stay where they are rather than being stranded. Until the launchpad settles it in writing, these stay null. 🔑 NOTHING IN CHOICE V2 PHASE 1 READS THIS GROUP - scripts 01, 02, 03, 07 and 08 are the whole DEX deploy and none of them touch the launchpad. Only 05 (settler), 09 (sink) and 10 (cranker) do, and those are the launchpad's phases. So this being unsettled does not block the AMM.

infinity-periphery 0a2aee8 carries upstream 9b026be ('Fix: exact output partial fills', PR #96), taken on 2026-09-07 BEFORE the first mainnet deploy precisely so this book never has to record a known-buggy router. This file exists so that the Choice v2 mainnet deploy is scriptable, dry-runnable and reviewable - MAINNET_READINESS C10 named its absence the practical blocker, because every script resolves NETWORK to it and `make sync` reported 0/56. meta.buildProfileWarning: 🔴 BUILD PERIPHERY WITH THE PERIPHERY'S OWN OPTIMIZER PROFILE, never the contracts/ workspace profile. `forge build --sizes` from this workspace reports CLPositionManager at 24,769 B - 193 B OVER EIP-170 - while the contract deployed on testnet is 24,004 B. Nothing is broken today; it becomes a failed deploy the day somebody builds it from here (MAINNET_READINESS C6).
broadcastDiscipline: ⛔ Never --slow: forge waits for a receipt and strands a multi-tx script after tx 1.

⛔ Never --resume: Injective answers eth_getTransactionReceipt with null for a tx it has already mined, so a broadcast routinely reports failure after the work landed. Confirm with eth_getCode and re-run the script from the top - every script is idempotent for exactly this reason.
🔴 eth_estimateGas UNDER-REPORTS on Injective. Pass an explicit, generous --gas-limit on every write.

🔴 A forge script cannot touch wINJ or any bank ERC20: precompile 0x64 has no code in REVM, so simulation dies and --skip-simulation does not save it. Make the script a calldata printer and send with cast send.
✅ But `cast call --from <admin>` DOES execute on the node, so every admin step can be dry-run for free. Do it.
